subject: french
source_note: Topic structure follows the National Curriculum KS3 programme of study for french. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Grammar & Vocabulary
units.blurb: The core grammar and vocabulary that underpin all four skills

units.name: Listening & Speaking
units.blurb: Understanding spoken language and communicating orally

units.name: Reading & Writing
units.blurb: Comprehending texts and expressing ideas in writing

topics.name: Tenses & Structures
topics.blurb: Conveying present, past and future and the structures that express them

topics.name: Grammatical Structures & Patterns
topics.blurb: Manipulating key patterns, including voices and moods

topics.name: Vocabulary
topics.blurb: A wide, deepening vocabulary that goes beyond immediate needs

topics.name: Accuracy: Spelling & Punctuation
topics.blurb: Using accurate grammar, spelling and punctuation

topics.name: Listening
topics.blurb: Obtaining information from spoken language and responding appropriately

topics.name: Transcription
topics.blurb: Writing down words and short sentences heard, with increasing accuracy

topics.name: Conversation & Spontaneous Speech
topics.blurb: Initiating and developing conversations, coping with the unexpected

topics.name: Pronunciation & Intonation
topics.blurb: Speaking coherently and confidently with accurate pronunciation

topics.name: Reading Comprehension
topics.blurb: Understanding authentic and adapted texts from a range of sources

topics.name: Literary Texts
topics.blurb: Reading stories, songs, poems and letters to develop creative expression

topics.name: Writing
topics.blurb: Expressing and developing ideas clearly and creatively in writing

topics.name: Translation
topics.blurb: Translating short texts accurately into and out of the language

connections.why: Knowing the tenses is the basis for manipulating wider grammatical patterns
Controlling structures is what makes spelling, agreement and punctuation accurate
A secure vocabulary supports correct spelling and word choice
Writing draws directly on tenses to convey when actions happen
A broad vocabulary lets pupils decode unfamiliar words in texts
Conversation depends on having the words to express and justify ideas
Transcribing what you hear builds on accurate listening
Clear pronunciation makes spoken conversation intelligible to others
Responding in conversation requires understanding what was said
Comprehension skills are extended by reading authentic literary texts
Translating into English rests on accurately comprehending the source
Translating into the language requires command of its grammatical patterns
Reading literature stimulates ideas and models for creative writing
Accurate translation depends on choosing the correct tense and structure
Transcribing accurately reinforces spelling and punctuation conventions
Richer vocabulary lets pupils write with greater range and precision
